zh: 打造一个营收团队是一个非常丰富的问题集。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's something that everyone cares about.
zh: 这是每个人都在乎的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: It could always be done better.
zh: 它总是可以做得更好。

en: What's the most exciting thing someone's doing with Lightfield today?
zh: 现在有人在用 Lightfield 做的最令人兴奋的事情是什么?

en: We have this company, Power.

speaker: Unknown
en: Where they're aggregating folks that have various illnesses and complications that are looking for frontier treatment.

speaker: Unknown
en: So they've modeled all of this in Lightfield and Lightfield actually helped someone with Alzheimer's find frontier treatment within days.
zh: 所以他们把这一切都在 Lightfield 里建模了,Lightfield 实际上帮助一位阿尔茨海默病患者在几天内找到了前沿疗法。

en: Is there anything that you've done differently in this kind of AI era?
zh: 在这种 AI 时代,你有没有做过什么不一样的事情?

en: As a CRM company in a red ocean space, we have to be an expansion company.
zh: 作为一家身处红海赛道的 CRM 公司,我们必须成为一家扩张型公司。

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: In this episode, A16Z's Alex Rampell and Joe Schmidt sit down with the Lightfield co-founder and CEO to unpack why he walked away from a fast-growing AI product and what he learned from the pivot.
zh: 在这一集里,A16Z 的 Alex Rampell 和 Joe Schmidt 与 Lightfield 的联合创始人兼 CEO 坐下来,探讨他为什么放弃一个快速增长的 AI 产品,以及他从这次转型中学到了什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: That journey led Keith to a problem inside the CRM.
zh: 那段旅程把 Keith 带到了 CRM 内部的一个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Companies have huge amounts of customer data spread across emails, meetings, product usage, and databases, but no single system that understands the full relationship.
zh: 公司有海量的客户数据分散在邮件、会议、产品使用和数据库中,但没有任何一个单一系统能理解完整的客户关系。

speaker: Unknown
en: They discuss Lightfield's approach to building a business world model, why Alex calls the shift intelligence is greater than schema, and how AI could rethink systems of record.
zh: 他们讨论了 Lightfield 构建商业世界模型的方法,为什么 Alex 把这种转变称为智能大于模式(schema),以及 AI 如何能重新构想记录系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: They also get into how AI is changing the way Keith builds and operates, and why his advice to founders is simple, ignore the noise, find real pain, and stay focused on customers.
zh: 他们还谈到 AI 正如何改变 Keith 构建和运营的方式,以及为什么他给创始人的建议很简单:忽略噪音,找到真实的痛点,并保持专注于客户。

speaker: Unknown
en: Welcome back to the A60Z Podcast.
zh: 欢迎回到 A60Z 播客。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm Joe Schmidt.
zh: 我是 Joe Schmidt。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm joined by my partner, Alex Rampell, and Keith Parris.
zh: 和我一起的是我的合伙人 Alex Rampell,以及 Keith Parris。

speaker: Unknown
en: Keith is the CEO at Lightfield.
zh: Keith 是 Lightfield 的 CEO。

speaker: Unknown
en: Lightfield just raised a $47 million Series A led by us, and they're building a business world model.
zh: Lightfield 刚刚完成了一轮 4700 万美元的 A 轮融资,由我们领投,他们正在构建一个商业世界模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: A business world model turns customer emails, calls, and meetings into a record that AI agents can use to get work done.
zh: 商业世界模型把客户的邮件、通话和会议转化为 AI 智能体可以用来完成工作的记录。

speaker: Unknown
en: We'll explore how Keith pivoted, which is very interesting to Lightfield, how they built the initial product, and what customers can do with it.
zh: 我们将探讨 Keith 是如何转型的——这一点非常有趣——转向 Lightfield,他们如何构建初始产品,以及客户能用它做什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: Keith, thanks for joining us.
zh: Keith,感谢你加入我们。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe we'll start just going back to the Tome journey and how you got to Lightfield.
zh: 也许我们可以先回到 Tome 的历程,以及你是怎么走到 Lightfield 的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Very atypical journey.
zh: 非常非典型的历程。

speaker: Unknown
en: You got two products now to explosive scale.
zh: 你现在已经有两款产品达到了爆发式的规模。

speaker: Unknown
en: Tell us a little bit about that experience and how you ended up at Lightfield.
zh: 跟我们讲讲那段经历,以及你是怎么最终到了 Lightfield。

speaker: Unknown
en: We started Tome mostly because we were consumer people and we thought LLMs were going to change the way people communicate.
zh: 我们创办 Tome 主要是因为我们原本是做消费级产品的人,我们认为 LLM 会改变人们沟通的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we were working on selfie design, you know, at Instagram and Messenger, and we decided to go into the storytelling of ideas.
zh: 我们当时在 Instagram 和 Messenger 做自拍设计,你知道吗,然后我们决定转向想法的叙事表达。

speaker: Unknown
en: We got this product out to launch around the time of GPT-3.
zh: 我们在 GPT-3 前后把这个产品推出去发布。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And tell us a little bit about the product.
zh: 跟我们讲讲这个产品吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it was a presentation product where you could use GPT to generate presentations and generate pages and so forth.
zh: 所以它是一个演示文稿产品,你可以用 GPT 来生成演示文稿、生成页面等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we launched it around the same time as ChatGPT.
zh: 我们在和 ChatGPT 大约相同的时间发布了它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we just got explosive growth.
zh: 然后我们就获得了爆发式增长。

speaker: Unknown
en: We got 2 million users a month.
zh: 我们每个月有 200 万用户。

speaker: Unknown
en: People were lining up when we didn't have enough inference to support them.
zh: 当我们的推理能力不足以支撑用户时,人们还在排队。

speaker: Unknown
en: Wow.
zh: 哇。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh my gosh.
zh: 我的天啊。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you got that to amazing scale.
zh: 所以你把它做到了惊人的规模。

speaker: Unknown
en: You then decided to stop and completely hard pivot.
zh: 然后你决定停下来,彻底硬转型。

speaker: Unknown
en: What was that decision like?
zh: 那个决定是怎样的?

speaker: Unknown
en: How'd you make that choice?
zh: 你是怎么做出那个选择的?

speaker: Unknown
en: Why?
zh: 为什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: So I'd say there are a lot of metrics behind it, but deep down, I think at an instinctual level, none of us like the product, which is kind of a funny thing to say.
zh: 所以我想说这背后有很多指标,但内心深处,我认为在本能层面上,我们没有人喜欢这个产品,这么说来有点好笑。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think at the end of the day, if you're a founder, you have to love the product that you're building and you have to be excited for your customers to use it.
zh: 我认为归根结底，如果你是一个创始人，你必须热爱你正在打造的产品，并且必须为你的客户使用它而感到兴奋。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we just couldn't for the life of us make good presentations.
zh: 而我们当时无论如何也做不出好的演示文稿。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what I mean by that is we could not see the path of...
zh: 我的意思是，我们看不到这样一条路径……

speaker: Unknown
en: A high-quality discerning presentation maker using this tool in an indispensable way.
zh: 一个高质量的、有辨别力的演示文稿制作者以不可或缺的方式使用这个工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: We couldn't see people like yourselves using it for memos.
zh: 我们看不到像你们这样的人用它来写备忘录。

speaker: Unknown
en: We couldn't see people using it in investment banking or consulting.
zh: 我们看不到人们在投资银行或咨询行业使用它。

speaker: Unknown
en: We just thought the technology constrained us to being a tool for individuals and students.
zh: 我们只是认为这项技术把我们限制成了一个面向个人和学生的工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: So interesting.
zh: 真有意思。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, so you go from AI presentations to...
zh: 好，所以你们从 AI 演示文稿转向了……

speaker: Unknown
en: Nothing.
zh: 什么都没有。

speaker: Unknown
en: So how did you make the choice of what to build?
zh: 那么你们是如何做出要构建什么的选择的？

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe if I can rewind a little bit.
zh: 也许我可以稍微倒回去一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, sometimes you get to this point and you're like, oh, well, if the technology kind of continues advancing, then it will be good enough.
zh: 我是说，有时候你会走到这一步，然后你会想，哦，好吧，如果技术持续进步的话，那它就会足够好了。

speaker: Unknown
en: But that's also a little bit of a danger.
zh: 但这也是一种小小的危险。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's called hopium.
zh: 这叫“希望成瘾”（hopium）。

speaker: Unknown
en: But how did you decide, I mean, this is probably the question that you were getting at, but like, why not just wait it out for the technology to get better?
zh: 但你们是怎么决定的，我是说，这大概就是你想问的问题，比如，为什么不干脆等技术变好呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: Because I mean, the leap between GPT-3 and GPT-6 with Astra is extraordinary.
zh: 因为我是说，从 GPT-3 到 GPT-6 配合 Astra 的飞跃是非凡的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But obviously, if you're burning money and everything, you don't have the luxury of waiting.
zh: 但显然，如果你在烧钱什么的，你没有等待的奢侈。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I guess, how did you think about just the shape of the curve and why not wait out the curve?
zh: 但我想问的是，你们是怎么看待这条曲线的形状的，为什么不等这条曲线走完？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, it's a good question.
zh: 是的，这是个好问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we definitely thought about let's shrink the team and wait it out because we were seeing 3.5 to 4 and seeing the leaps being made.
zh: 所以我们确实考虑过缩小团队然后等待，因为我们看到了 3.5 到 4 的进步，看到了那些飞跃。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think the biggest issue was that the model just didn't have enough context to really understand the presenter, the audience, the relationship between the presenter and the audience and no amount of general reasoning gets you past that.
zh: 但我认为最大的问题是，模型根本没有足够的上下文去真正理解演讲者、听众、演讲者和听众之间的关系，而再多的通用推理也无法让你跨过这道坎。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we were like, this is going to be at best a great tool for a one shot pie in the sky presentation.
zh: 所以我们想，这充其量只能成为一个做一次性、不切实际的演示文稿的好工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we just couldn't figure out how to turn that into something that we were excited about.
zh: 而我们实在想不出怎么把它变成让我们感到兴奋的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: How did you think about the problems that you wanted to attack next?
zh: 你们是怎么考虑接下来要攻克的问题的？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the hardest part of what you just said and the most painful part is none of us liked the product.
zh: 我觉得你刚才说的话里最难的部分、最痛苦的部分，就是我们没有人喜欢这个产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's hard if that's your entire life.
zh: 如果那是你的全部人生，那会很难受。

speaker: Unknown
en: How did you decide what was the product you actually wanted to build?
zh: 你们是怎么决定你们真正想打造的产品是什么的？

speaker: Unknown
en: What was that process like?
zh: 那个过程是什么样的？

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think we...
zh: 所以我想我们……

speaker: Unknown
en: We had a lot of conversations internally about how, wait a minute, why did we even build this company?
zh: 我们内部进行了很多对话，讨论怎么，等一下，我们当初到底为什么要创建这家公司？

speaker: Unknown
en: We built this company because we wanted to help professionals tell expert stories, hard stories.
zh: 我们创建这家公司是因为我们想帮助专业人士讲述专业的故事、艰难的故事。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we were like, let's see if we can find the B2B use case.
zh: 所以我们就想，让我们看看能不能找到 B2B 的用例。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we sort of looked at our user base.
zh: 于是我们查看了我们的用户群。

speaker: Unknown
en: We had 25 million users or something, and we found that the B2B users were sales and marketing.
zh: 我们有大约 2500 万用户之类，然后我们发现 B2B 用户是销售和市场营销。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yep.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we reached out to them.
zh: 于是我们联系了他们。

speaker: Unknown
en: We went and got 12 pilots from call it like 500,000 person companies around here.
zh: 我们从这一带大约 50 万人的公司那里拿到了 12 个试点。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we're like, hey, we'll do this for free.
zh: 我们说，嘿，我们免费为你们做。

speaker: Unknown
en: We'll do great presentations for you and let's see where it goes.
zh: 我们为你们做出色的演示文稿，然后看看会走向哪里。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we ended up being used by a couple of sales teams.
zh: 结果我们最终被几个销售团队使用。

speaker: Unknown
en: And at first we came in with, we'll make your new business decks or we'll make your proposals.
zh: 一开始我们提出的方案是，我们为你们做新业务演示文稿，或者做你们的提案。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we're like, wait a minute, while you're here, can you do other things?
zh: 然后他们说，等一下，既然你们来了，能不能做点别的？

speaker: Unknown
en: Can you guys do some research?
zh: 你们能做一些调研吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Can you help us qualify leads?
zh: 你们能帮我们筛选销售线索吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Can you help us understand companies for expansion?
zh: 你们能帮我们了解公司以便拓展吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: And at that point we were like...
zh: 到那个时候我们就想……

speaker: Unknown
en: Sure, let's just follow the heat, see what happens.
zh: 当然，我们就跟着热度走，看看会发生什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think what makes early-stage founders good at this is that you sort of have no priors.
zh: 我认为让早期创始人擅长这件事的原因是，你基本上没有任何先入之见。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're willing to ignore the thing you built, and we're like, let's just follow this trail and see where it goes.
zh: 你愿意忽略你自己造出来的东西，我们就说，那就顺着这条线索走下去，看看它会通向哪里。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then the first thing we asked was like, oh, just give us access to your context box, which at the time I thought was Salesforce.
zh: 然后我们问的第一件事就是，哦，让我们访问一下你的 context box,当时我以为那是 Salesforce。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we're like, great, give us access to your CRM, your call recorder, your data warehouse, more, and then we'll figure out how to do this work for you.
zh: 于是我们说，好，给我们访问你的 CRM、你的通话录音器、你的数据仓库等等，然后我们会想出怎么替你做这些工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then we realized that actually the hardest part of doing this work was actually making sense of all of the data across all of these disparate systems.
zh: 接着我们意识到，做这项工作最难的部分，其实是从所有这些互不相连的系统里把所有数据理出个头绪。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it was sort of incomplete.
zh: 而且这些数据有点不完整。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was conflicting.
zh: 它们互相矛盾。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, the call recorder often had a different view of reality than the CRM.
zh: 你知道，通话录音器往往对现实有着和 CRM 不同的认知。

speaker: Unknown
en: Actually, the work required to reorganize it felt like the most important work.
zh: 其实，把这些数据重新组织所需的工作，感觉才是最重要的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think through that, we started to realize, wait a minute, maybe this is the more interesting problem to solve, which is that if you can
zh: 我想正是通过这一点，我们开始意识到，等一下，也许这才是更有意思的待解问题，那就是，如果你能

speaker: Unknown
en: Reorganize reality for a company in a way that machines can understand and also for humans to understand.
zh: 以一种机器能理解、同时人类也能理解的方式，为一家公司重组现实。

speaker: Unknown
en: That feels like a way more interesting and enduring company than the one that we're on right now.
zh: 那感觉就像是一个比我们现在做的这家有意思得多、也更能长久的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是啊。

speaker: Unknown
en: When did you know that you were on to something with the new product?
zh: 你是什么时候知道新产品有了眉目的？

speaker: Unknown
en: So there's a little bit of discontinuity.
zh: 所以这里面有一点不连续性。

speaker: Unknown
en: We didn't know we wanted a CRM first.
zh: 我们一开始并不知道要先做 CRM。

speaker: Unknown
en: First we built a go-to-market assistant.
zh: 最先我们做了一个 go-to-market 助手。

speaker: Unknown
en: We got people to like it and then we couldn't get anyone to pay for it.
zh: 我们让人们喜欢上了它，然后却没人愿意为它付钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's tough to say that we had all of these AEs using it every day, but we had no pricing power because it wasn't our data.
zh: 这话很难说出口：我们有这么多 AE 每天都在用它，但我们毫无定价权，因为数据不是我们的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there were 10 other companies and all of these companies competing for it.
zh: 而且还有另外 10 家公司，所有这些公司都在竞争这个领域。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we decided to shrink the team, start from scratch and go and reimagine the CRM from first principles.
zh: 于是我们决定缩减团队，从零开始，从第一性原理出发重新构想 CRM。

speaker: Unknown
en: That I think we built in the dark for about four months.
zh: 我想我们埋头做了大约四个月。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then we needed to find people to use our CRM.
zh: 然后我们需要找到人来用我们的 CRM。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it turns out no one wants to use your four month old CRM.
zh: 结果发现，没人想用一个才做了四个月的 CRM。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we sort of looked at the only asset we had left, which was this giant office space we couldn't get rid of.
zh: 于是我们看了看手里唯一剩下的资产，就是那个我们甩不掉的巨大办公空间。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we were like,
zh: 然后我们就说，

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm going to post on X on LinkedIn.
zh: 我要在 X 上、LinkedIn 上发个帖。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can sit in our office space if you use our CRM.
zh: 你可以用我们的办公空间，只要你用我们的 CRM。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then we found 10— Negative pricing.
zh: 然后我们找到了 10 个—— 负定价。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, yeah, exactly.
zh: 对，对，就是这个意思。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we found 10 startups to come use the product.
zh: 所以我们找到了 10 家初创公司来用这个产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: And for some reason, they were in it every day.
zh: 而且不知为什么，他们每天都泡在里面。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they were mad about everything missing.
zh: 他们对一切缺失的东西都很有意见。

speaker: Unknown
en: They were mad about how slow it was, but they were in it every day and they were giving us Slack feedback about it every two hours.
zh: 他们嫌它慢，但他们每天都泡在里面，每两个小时就通过 Slack 给我们反馈。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's like, oh, this is so different than Tome in the sense that we have this barely working, barely finished product that people are in all the time where they care about it so much they're going to give us feedback about it on an hourly basis.
zh: 这就让我觉得，哦，这和 Tome 完全不同，我们有一个勉强能跑、勉强算完成的产品，人们却整天泡在里面，他们在乎到每小时都会给我们反馈。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是啊。

speaker: Unknown
en: Did you start off saying, I've used Salesforce and HubSpot and other things, and here's what I want changed?
zh: 你一开始是不是说，我用过 Salesforce 和 HubSpot 以及其他产品，这是我想要改变的地方？

speaker: Unknown
en: Or I guess, how did you triangulate on the job to be done?
zh: 还是说，你是怎么定位要完成的工作(job to be done)的？

speaker: Unknown
en: Because in one hand, like a CRM is just a repository, right?
zh: 因为一方面，CRM 就是一个存储库，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like customers.
zh: 就像是客户。

speaker: Unknown
en: Customer Relationship Manageable.
zh: 客户关系管理。

speaker: Unknown
en: Here's the repository of all the information, all the customer information.
